rubric: Line one: a verdict (likely a scam, suspicious, likely genuine, cannot tell) with the strongest reason; then only the signs really present in the message.

Do-now steps in order (do not click, pay or install; contact the company through the number on the card or the official app; block; change passwords; call the bank fast if money went; keep screenshots).
An 'if you already clicked, paid or shared' path without shaming; the pattern named (romance, investment, tech-support call) where it applies.
Security questions get 3 to 5 steps with where the setting is, and the simplest habits (long unique passwords, a password manager, two-step login on email and bank first, updates).
Never asks for or accepts a password, code or card number; no invented phone numbers, URLs or company policies; one rule for next time.

prompts.text: I got a call from 'my bank' saying there's fraud on my account and they need me to move my money to a safe account they'll set up. They knew my name and the last 4 digits of my card. Is this real?
SMS: 'Hallo Mama, mein Handy ist kaputt, das ist meine neue Nummer. Kannst du mir kurz 850 Euro überweisen, ich erkläre es später.' Mein Sohn ist 24. Was soll ich tun?
وصلتني رسالة بريد إلكتروني من 'أرامكس' تقول إن طردي محتجز ويجب دفع 15 ريالًا عبر رابط. هل هذا احتيال؟
I clicked a link in an email from 'PayPal' and entered my password before I realised. What do I do now?
How do I set up good passwords and that two-step thing? I have about 30 accounts and use the same password for most of them. I'm not technical.
Ein Mann, den ich seit 3 Monaten online kenne, ist Ingenieur auf einer Ölplattform und braucht jetzt 2.000 Euro für ein Ticket, um mich zu besuchen. Meine Tochter sagt, das ist Betrug. Ist es das?
A job offer by WhatsApp: 300 a day for liking videos, they want 50 as a 'registration fee' first. Real?
